definition: The selected witness is the 2023 Paramount feature Dungeons & Dragons: Honor Among Thieves, with a stated runtime of 134 minutes.
cultural_caution: This film-continuity label excludes tabletop rules, prior films, novels, games, and all other D&D continuities unless a selected official film source expressly says an element appears in this film.

definition: Paramount's official synopsis says a charming thief and unlikely adventurers undertake an epic heist to retrieve a lost relic, then run afoul of the wrong people.
cultural_caution: This is a fictional film premise only. It does not establish real criminal conduct, intent, law, violence, moral worth, or tabletop quest mechanics.

supports: The film's thief, adventurer, epic-heist, lost-relic, and danger premise.

canonical_term: bard, barbarian, paladin, sorcerer, and druid film labels
original_language: English official Dungeons & Dragons film-promotion terms
definition: The official film article calls Edgin a bard, Holga a barbarian, Xenk a paladin, Simon a sorcerer, and Doric a druid.
cultural_caution: These are role labels in an official film-promotion article. They are not film-proven stat blocks, spell lists, ability scores, species, real occupations, racial/ethnic identities, bodies, disabilities, genders, spiritual practices, or moral categories.

supports: The five named film-promotion role labels.

canonical_term: Forgotten Realms, locations, and film-referenced D&D lore
original_language: English official Dungeons & Dragons article terms
definition: The official D&D article says the film takes place in the Forgotten Realms and references Neverwinter, Waterdeep, Icewind Dale, and the Underdark as film locations; it separately says certain monsters, spells, and the Red Wizards of Thay appear.
cultural_caution: These are film-referenced setting terms, not character nodes and not a license to import tabletop setting history, monster statistics, spell mechanics, faction lore, or non-film continuity.

citations.locator: Where Does the Movie Take Place?; What D&D Lore Will We See?
supports: Forgotten Realms setting, named locations, and the article's film-appearance list for selected lore terms.

original_language: English official Dungeons & Dragons article terms
definition: The official D&D article presents the Thieves' Gallery stat blocks, legendary magic items, digital dice, and an isolated adventure as supplemental material for use at a table, distinct from the film.
cultural_caution: This is an adaptation boundary: supplemental game content is not used to supply film mechanics, powers, species, artifacts, relationships, events, or character ontology.

citations.locator: Expand Your Games With Movie Characters, Magic Items, and More!; Prisoner 13
supports: The article's designation of game supplements and its statement that Prisoner 13 is isolated from the film plot.

canonical_term: violence, death, imprisonment, parent/child, body/species, disability, race/ethnicity, and rules-adaptation evidence boundary
definition: The selected official materials establish a dangerous action/adventure heist, party roles, an opposing nobleman, and separate tabletop supplements. They do not establish individual death, imprisonment, parent/child relationships, body/species portrayal, disability, race/ethnicity, or a rules-to-film conversion for these records.
cultural_caution: This is an evidence boundary, not a denial of material elsewhere in the film or franchise. It prevents generic promotional language and tabletop support products from becoming unsupported real-world identity, clinical, legal, harm, family, or mechanics claims.

citations.locator: Who Is Starring?; Expand Your Games With Movie Characters, Magic Items, and More!
supports: Official role labels and separation of game supplements from the film witness.
